# Recovery-extension conformance vectors

[`x402-recovery-control12.json`](x402-recovery-control12.json) is a crash
vector set for control 12 of the proposed x402 recovery extension
([x402-foundation/x402#3848](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/pull/3848)),
in the format proposed there: one object per vector, implementation-agnostic.

Each vector is one scenario. A server takes a signed payment and dies just
`before` or just `after` one of its journal writes. A second server starts over
the same journal `restartAfterSeconds` later, runs its recovery sweep, and the
caller retries the **same** payment. `expect` is what happened.

The file is generated by Detent's test suite, not written by hand. The test
(`x402 recovery control 12` in [`test/x402.test.ts`](../test/x402.test.ts))
re-runs every scenario on each test run and fails if the file no longer matches
what the code does. To regenerate it after a deliberate change:

```bash
npm run vectors
```

## Fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `journalWrite` | The write the first server died at, in the spec's fixed vocabulary (below). |
| `boundary` | `before`: died before the write reached the journal. `after`: the write is durable and the server died before acting on it. |
| `railOnRestart` | What the restarted server finds on the payment rail. `landed` / `not_landed`: the rail answers, and the authorization was / was not used. `unreachable`: the rail cannot be read (the settlement oracle fails). The facilitator still accepts new settles; only the read side is down. |
| `restartAfterSeconds` | When the second server starts and the caller retries. 180 s, above Detent's stale-claim timeout (`staleMs`, 120 s in these tests), so the timer is exercised. |
| `expect.handlerRuns` | Times the paid handler ran, both servers together. |
| `expect.settleCalls` | Settle requests sent to the facilitator, both servers together. |
| `expect.charges` | Authorizations used **on the rail**, counted by the test rail itself, not by the server. |
| `expect.retryStatus` | HTTP status of the caller's retry at `restartAfterSeconds`. |
| `expect.retryReplaysStoredResponse` | That retry got the response stored by the first server, without the handler running again. |
| `expect.retryAfter` | Whether that retry carried a `Retry-After` header. |
| `expect.state` | The payment's final state once its authorization deadline has passed and reconciliation has finished: `delivered`, `void` or `stuck`. |
| `expect.keyBlocked` | Whether the payment still cannot be used for new paid work at the end. Only `void` frees it. |

## Detent's journal writes, in the spec's vocabulary

A normal x402 payment through Detent makes seven journal writes, in this order:

| # | Spec name | Detent's write |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `claim` | `open`: the invoice is created in `quoted`; the atomic claim. |
| 2 | `staged` | `quoted → producing`: the claim is taken and the handler is about to run. Nothing has been settled. |
| 3 | `response_saved` | The handler's response is stored, before any money is asked for. |
| 4 | `settling` | `producing → settling`: the write-ahead marker, durable **before** the facilitator is called. |
| 5 | `settle_result` | The facilitator's settle response is stored. |
| 6 | `delivered` | `settling → delivered`. |
| 7 | `receipt` | The signed receipt is appended to the receipt chain. |

## What the vectors show

Every row holds the control-10 invariant: at most one charge, at most one
handler run, and a charge only where the payment ends `delivered`. The single
exception is the case the spec reserves `stuck` for: the settle landed, the
server died before recording anything about it, and the rail cannot be read.
That payment stays blocked, retries get `409` with `Retry-After` while it might
still resolve, and an operator is alarmed.

A fresh `402` appears only where nothing moved and the payment ends `void`:
the server died before its `settling` marker, so the stale claim was closed.

Two behaviours worth reading closely:

- **`settling` / `after`.** The marker is durable but the settle was never sent.
  The caller's retry of the same payment finishes the original settle: one
  settle call, one charge, the stored response returned. Without a retry,
  reconciliation ends `void` once the authorization expires, as control 11
  requires.
- **`settle_result` / `before` / `not_landed`** (the last vector). The first
  settle went out and never returned, and the payment did not land. The retry
  sends a second settle for the **same** authorization (`settleCalls: 2`).
  This cannot charge twice: an EIP-3009 authorization can be used once, so the
  second settle either completes the one payment or fails.

## Found while generating these

Producing this set turned up two recovery gaps in Detent, fixed in the same
change:

- A server that died after storing a successful settle but before marking the
  payment delivered ended `stuck` when the rail could not be read, although the
  stored result was enough to deliver. It now delivers from that record.
- A claim that died right after opening held the caller at `409` until the
  payment's deadline, because the opening entry is dated by that deadline. The
  caller's retry now closes it after the normal stale timeout. (The background
  sweep still finds such a claim only at the deadline; no money moves either
  way.)
